people.name: Jay Gambetta
people.role: Director of Research and IBM Fellow
people.focus: Superconducting systems, quantum error correction, and the Qiskit ecosystem.
people.contribution: Helped shape IBM’s quantum architecture, software ecosystem, and research strategy. IBM Quantum’s processors are developed by a broad engineering and research team.

people.name: Hartmut Neven
people.focus: Building useful, error-corrected quantum computers with superconducting hardware.
people.contribution: Founded Google’s quantum computing program. The linked cultivation experiment is work by the Google Quantum AI team, including source authors Emma Rosenfeld and Craig Gidney.

people.name: Emma Rosenfeld
people.focus: Experimental quantum error correction and magic-state cultivation.
people.contribution: Coauthored Google’s October 2026 account of cultivation on Willow with Craig Gidney. The report describes experimental benchmarking and noise-control work behind the result.

people.name: Chetan Nayak
people.role: Technical Fellow; quantum hardware research leader
people.focus: Topological quantum matter, Majorana devices, and fault-tolerant architectures.
people.contribution: Works on Microsoft’s topological-qubit approach and its hardware roadmap. Device performance and scaling statements in company announcements are attributed to Microsoft.

people.name: Mikhail Lukin
people.role: University Professor; quantum science and engineering researcher
people.focus: Quantum optics, atom arrays, quantum networks, and low-overhead error correction.
people.contribution: His group studies controllable quantum systems and strategies for logical operations with lower error-correction overhead. The linked phantom-code study is collaborative theoretical and simulation work.

people.name: Stephanie Wehner
people.organization: QuTech · TU Delft · Quantum Internet Alliance
people.role: Professor of quantum information; QIA director
people.focus: Quantum networks, cryptography, and a programmable quantum internet.
people.contribution: Coordinates a European collaboration connecting quantum-network hardware, software, and applications. QIA’s prototype is a consortium effort spanning universities, research institutes, and industry.

people.name: Michelle Simmons
people.role: Scientia Professor; founder and CEO of SQC
people.focus: Atomically precise silicon devices, spin qubits, and application-specific quantum computing.
people.contribution: Leads silicon quantum hardware research and SQC’s translation of that technology into applications. The linked energy project is a partnership with Schneider Electric.

people.name: William D. Oliver
people.role: Professor of Physics and Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
people.focus: Superconducting qubit materials, fabrication, integration, control, and measurement.
people.contribution: Studies the engineering needed to scale superconducting processors. He is a coauthor of the linked 2026 fluxonium and bosonic error-correction preprint.

people.name: Jelena Vučković
people.organization: Stanford · Nanoscale and Quantum Photonics Lab
people.role: Professor of Electrical Engineering; quantum photonics group leader
people.focus: Nanophotonics, solid-state emitters, cavity QED, and photonic inverse design.
people.contribution: Her group develops interfaces between semiconductor quantum systems and photons. She coauthored the linked 2026 diamond nanophotonics result.

people.name: Ana Maria Rey
people.role: JILA Fellow and Professor Adjoint of Physics
people.focus: Many-body quantum systems, entanglement, quantum simulation, and precision sensing.
people.contribution: With James Thompson and collaborators, studies entangled states that can reject shared noise while remaining sensitive to differences between sensors.

people.name: NVIDIA Quantum team
people.role: Quantum software and GPU integration team
people.focus: Hybrid quantum-classical computing, simulation, orchestration, and resource estimation.
people.contribution: Develops CUDA-Q with hardware builders and laboratories. Its September 2026 release describes CUDA-Q Logical and the integration of Sandia’s QUOPS benchmark.

people.name: National Quantum Mission hubs
people.organization: DST · IISc · IIT Madras · IIT Bombay · IIT Delhi
people.role: India’s four thematic quantum research hubs
people.focus: Computing, communication, sensing and metrology, and quantum materials and devices.
people.contribution: IISc hosts computing; IIT Madras with C-DOT hosts communication; IIT Bombay hosts sensing and metrology; IIT Delhi hosts materials and devices. The hubs connect institutions and project teams across India.

projects.name: IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2
projects.collaborators: IBM Quantum engineering and research teams; the source is authored by Holger Haas, David McKay, and Robert Davis.
projects.summary: A superconducting processor platform focused on faster circuit execution, qubit reset, and dynamic-circuit research.
projects.evidence: IBM’s August 2026 report says Nighthawk r2 is available through its platform and describes improved circuit throughput and reset behavior. These performance statements are IBM-reported results.
projects.question: How do reset performance, gate quality, and connectivity affect useful circuit depth? Nighthawk availability is separate from IBM’s future fault-tolerant roadmap.

source.title: IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2—more circuits, faster

projects.name: Magic-state cultivation on Willow
projects.collaborators: Google Quantum AI team; source authors Emma Rosenfeld and Craig Gidney, building on work by Gidney, Noah Shutty, Cody Jones, and collaborators.
projects.summary: Experimental preparation of high-quality magic states, a resource needed for operations beyond Clifford circuits in fault-tolerant computing.
projects.evidence: Google’s October 15 report describes cultivation and code switching on Willow, with a linked Science publication. The account also says larger-scale demonstrations and further engineering are still needed.
projects.question: Can state preparation and transfer scale while keeping the error rate and hardware overhead low?

source.title: Bringing the magic: Google breaks open a bottleneck in quantum computing
source.kind: Company research report · links to Science

projects.name: Majorana topological-qubit research
projects.collaborators: Microsoft Quantum materials, device, theory, and engineering teams.
projects.summary: A materials and device program pursuing topological qubits and architectures for fault-tolerant computation.
projects.evidence: Microsoft’s Majorana 2 announcement describes a revised material stack and reports improved device performance, with a linked technical preprint. The page does not display a publication date.
projects.question: What independent measurements establish the device’s operating regime, logical performance, and a credible path to scale? Company-reported device claims and future delivery targets are not a completed fault-tolerant computer.

projects.name: Low-overhead logical gates with phantom codes
projects.collaborators: Jin Ming Koh, Anqi Gong, Andrei C. Diaconu, Daniel Bochen Tan, Alexandra A. Geim, Michael J. Gullans, Norman Y. Yao, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Shayan Majidy.
projects.summary: A theoretical and simulation study of error-correcting codes that implement certain logical entangling operations through relabeling during compilation.
projects.evidence: The January 2026 preprint reports code constructions and end-to-end noisy simulations. The group lists reducing error-correction overhead as a research direction; this entry does not claim a hardware implementation.
projects.question: Which code families and workloads keep their overhead benefits under realistic state preparation, decoding, and noise?

source.title: Entangling logical qubits without physical operations

projects.name: Quantum Internet Alliance prototype
projects.collaborators: A consortium of more than 50 European organizations, including universities, institutes, telecom operators, companies, and startups.
projects.summary: A full-stack prototype intended to connect metropolitan quantum networks through a long-distance fiber link and run programmable quantum-network applications.
projects.evidence: QuTech’s October 16, 2026 announcement describes the next 3.5-year phase and new European Commission funding. The connected full-stack prototype is the program’s goal, rather than an already delivered network.
projects.question: How can entanglement distribution, network control, and application software work together over practical distances?

source.title: QuTech coordinates European effort to build a full-stack quantum internet prototype

projects.name: Quantum-enhanced energy forecasting
projects.collaborators: SQC and Schneider Electric, with Australian Critical Technologies Challenge Program support.
projects.summary: A Stage 2 application project exploring quantum-enhanced AI for household energy forecasting and integration with existing AI workflows.
projects.evidence: SQC’s October 7 announcement describes funding to extend its Watermelon-based forecasting work to larger production-scale datasets. Earlier accuracy improvements are company-reported comparisons, not a general quantum advantage.
projects.question: Do forecasting improvements remain reproducible across larger datasets, operational constraints, and strong classical baselines?

source.title: Government and Industry Back Quantum-Enhanced AI for the Energy Grid

projects.name: Bosonic error correction with fluxonium
projects.collaborators: Shantanu R. Jha and collaborators, including William D. Oliver; see the paper for full authorship and affiliations.
projects.summary: A planar superconducting architecture pairing a fluxonium control qubit with an on-chip resonator for bosonic quantum error correction.
projects.evidence: The September 2026 preprint reports GKP-state preparation and measurement-free error correction. This is an experimental preprint, with a September 30 revision, rather than a confirmed peer-reviewed publication.
projects.question: Can resonator quality, control, and fabrication scale while preserving a logical-lifetime benefit?

projects.name: Diamond spin–photon interfaces
projects.organization: Stanford Nanoscale and Quantum Photonics Lab · collaborators
projects.collaborators: Hope Lee, Hannah C. Kleidermacher, Abigail J. M. Stein, Jelena Vučković, and collaborators across Stanford, UCSB, Sandia, and other institutions.
projects.summary: A semiconductor quantum-systems research program integrating diamond color centers with nanophotonic structures for efficient spin–photon interfaces.
projects.evidence: A Physical Review Applied paper published April 27, 2026 reports a nanophotonic interface for tin-vacancy centers in thin-film diamond. It is a recent result within the broader program, not a complete quantum network.
projects.question: How can emitter quality, photon collection, readout fidelity, and fabrication yield improve together?

source.title: Quantum nanophotonic interface for tin-vacancy centers in thin-film diamond

projects.name: Entangled sensors that reject shared noise
projects.collaborators: Ana Maria Rey, James K. Thompson, Raphael Kaubruegger, and collaborators at the Niels Bohr Institute, Joint Quantum Institute, and IIT Madras.
projects.summary: A theoretical approach using entangled atomic ensembles to sense differences between nodes while rejecting disturbances common to both.
projects.evidence: JILA’s June 10, 2026 report describes proposed Lieb–Mattis states and preparation methods, linked to a Physical Review X paper. Experimental demonstration is identified as a next step.
projects.question: Can the proposed states be prepared and maintained in an experiment while retaining a useful differential-sensing advantage?

source.title: A new kind of entanglement helps quantum sensors tune out noise

projects.name: CUDA-Q Logical & QUOPS workflows
projects.collaborators: NVIDIA’s quantum team, Fermilab, Sandia National Laboratories, and participating hardware and software organizations.
projects.summary: Software orchestration for designing and evaluating fault-tolerant architectures and applications alongside GPU computing.
projects.evidence: NVIDIA’s September 14, 2026 announcement introduces CUDA-Q Logical and describes Sandia’s QUOPS benchmark in CUDA-Q. Reported development-time improvements refer to specific workflows, not a general QPU speedup.
projects.question: How do algorithm choice, error-correction codes, hardware architecture, and classical compute change total resource requirements?

source.title: NVIDIA expands open-source CUDA-Q for fault-tolerant quantum computing

projects.name: India’s National Quantum Mission
projects.organization: Department of Science & Technology · four thematic hubs
projects.collaborators: IISc Bengaluru; IIT Madras with C-DOT; IIT Bombay; IIT Delhi; participating research institutions and project teams.
projects.summary: A public research mission spanning quantum computing, communication, sensing and metrology, and materials and devices, with a 2023–24 to 2030–31 program period.
projects.evidence: DST’s current program page lists the four established thematic hubs and their roles. Computing, network, and sensor deliverables are mission objectives; the page is undated and is not evidence that all targets have been completed.
projects.question: How can the hubs translate shared research infrastructure, device development, and training into measurable technology milestones?

source.title: National Quantum Mission (NQM) — program and thematic hubs
